abstract: Elucidating the mechanisms underlying vascular injury and repair may guide development of therapies against vascular cognitive impairment and dementia (VD). We employed single-cell RNA sequencing to map cell populations and explore vascular responses in mouse brains collected 42 days after asymmetric common carotid artery stenosis (ACAS)-induced chronic cerebral hypoperfusion. A unique tip cell type was identified among endothelial cell (EC) clusters and validated by immunostaining. Gene Ontology analyses suggested tip cell enrichment in angiogenesis and the involvement of Apln/Aplnr signaling. Immunoblotting confirmed an increase in apelin (Apln) protein after ACAS. In EC cultures, [Pyr1]-Apelin-13 (Apln13), a selective endogenous apelin receptor agonist, enhanced EC proliferation, migration, and tube formation. Treatment with Apln13 also improved angiogenesis, white matter integrity, and cognitive functions in ACAS mice. Cell-cell interaction analyses highlighted astrocyte-tip cell crosstalk via Vegfa-Vegfr interactions.
